purpose: Cases where the correct output is that the cause cannot be determined. Each one is built so that a plausible answer is available and wrong: the record supports two or more mechanisms and contains nothing that separates them. They are scored for abstention correctness and false attribution, and deliberately kept out of the coverage denominator, because real traffic is not one fifth undeterminable and a metric that claims otherwise is lying.

scenarios.name: two-confirmations-two-references
scenarios.title: The bank confirmed twice, under two different references

candidatesConsidered.evidence: two confirmations, but the guard did not mark either as a duplicate and the references differ
two references could be two payments, and one payout does not prove otherwise
banks do re-reference a single payment, and nothing here says this one did

scenarios.demoNote: The one to show next to PXE-009. That case differs by a single field, duplicateOf, and is explained instantly by a rule with no model call. Remove the field and the same shape becomes undeterminable. A system that answers both confidently is guessing on one of them.

scenarios.name: captured-more-than-authorized
scenarios.title: Captured more than was authorized

candidatesConsidered.evidence: no amendment event was recorded, and one would be
plausible for this merchant category, and nothing in the record marks it
indistinguishable from a legitimate over-capture using only these hops

scenarios.demoNote: The mirror of PXE-008. Capturing less than the authorization is a rule; capturing more is not, and the reason is that the record does not say why. The rule catalogue is correct to stay silent.

scenarios.name: debited-then-nothing-at-all
scenarios.title: Debited, and then the switch said nothing at all

candidatesConsidered.evidence: consistent, and so is every other candidate
no response code was returned, so nothing points at the beneficiary bank rather than the switch
an absence is not evidence for whichever cause is most plausible

scenarios.demoNote: The one to show next to PXE-011. That case has code 96, which is a fact about where it broke; strip the code and the same debit without a credit stops being attributable. The difference between the two is one field, and the system treats them differently because of it.

scenarios.name: batch-says-included-payout-never-came
scenarios.title: The batch says it went, the payout never arrived

candidatesConsidered.evidence: the batch closed reporting the payment included, which is what a truncated file would also report
no rejection was returned, and a freeze would usually produce one
no payout event of any kind exists, which is equally consistent with all three

scenarios.demoNote: The mirror of PXE-006. There the batch reported included=false and a rule explains the whole three-day stall. Flip that one field to true and the record stops saying where the money went. Beat 11 works better with two of these than with one.
